findings.summary: The scissor implementation in VulkanMod does not account for ModelView matrix transformations. When GUI elements are scaled or transformed, the scissor rectangle clips the wrong area because it operates in untransformed screen coordinates while the geometry is transformed.
findings.root_cause: Scissor coordinates are passed directly to vkCmdSetScissor() without applying the current ModelView matrix transformation.

scissor_entry_points.method: setScissor(int x, int y, int width, int height)
scissor_entry_points.issue: Directly passes screen coordinates to vkCmdSetScissor without matrix transformation

scissor_entry_points.method: enableScissor(int i, int j, int k, int l)
scissor_entry_points.issue: Stores raw scissor coordinates in ScissorState without transformation
Applies scissor using untransformed coordinates from ScissorState

scissor_entry_points.method: _scissorBox(int x, int y, int width, int height)
scissor_entry_points.issue: Directly forwards scissor box to Renderer without transformation

matrix_handling.note: ModelView matrix is stored but not used for scissor transformation
ModelView matrix is applied to geometry but scissor uses untransformed coordinates

current_behavior.description: Scissor coordinates are treated as screen-space pixel coordinates
flow: 1. Caller (e.g., GuiRenderer) calls enableScissor(x, y, w, h) with screen coordinates
3. VkCommandEncoder.trySetup() retrieves coordinates and calls GlStateManager._scissorBox()
5. Renderer.setScissor() calls vkCmdSetScissor() with raw coordinates

required_behavior.description: Scissor coordinates must be transformed by the current ModelView matrix
required_behavior.rationale: When GUI scaling or transformations are applied, the scissor rectangle must follow the transformed geometry
solution_approach: Option A: Transform scissor coordinates in Renderer.setScissor() using current ModelView matrix
Option B: Transform scissor coordinates in VkRenderPass.enableScissor() before storing
Option C: Pass matrix to scissor calls and transform at Vulkan command submission time

transformation_math.description: Scissor rectangle corners must be transformed by ModelView matrix
transformation_math.input: Scissor box: (x, y, width, height) in screen coordinates
transformation_math.operation: Multiply each corner by ModelView matrix to get transformed coordinates
transformation_math.output: Compute bounding box of transformed corners for vkCmdSetScissor

INV-A.description: Scissor coordinates must be in framebuffer-space pixels
INV-A.notes: Current implementation correctly uses pixel coordinates

INV-B.description: Scissor must be axis-aligned in framebuffer space
INV-B.notes: After matrix transformation, scissor corners are computed and axis-aligned bounding box is used. This is a conservative approximation that ensures content is never clipped prematurely.

INV-C.description: Scissor Y-coordinate must account for Vulkan's inverted Y
INV-C.notes: Renderer.setScissor() correctly flips Y: framebufferHeight - (y + height)

INV-D.description: Scissor must respect current ModelView transformation
INV-D.notes: FIXED: Renderer.setScissor() now retrieves ModelView matrix from VRenderSystem and transforms all 4 scissor corners before computing the final scissor bounds.

changes.method_modified: Renderer.setScissor(int x, int y, int width, int height)
algorithm: 2. Define 4 corners of scissor rectangle as Vector4f
3. Transform each corner using ModelView matrix
4. Compute min/max X and Y from transformed corners
5. Convert to integer bounds with clamping to non-negative values

recommended_fix.approach: Transform scissor coordinates using current ModelView matrix in Renderer.setScissor()
implementation_steps: 1. In Renderer.setScissor(), retrieve current ModelView matrix from VRenderSystem
2. Transform the 4 corners of the scissor rectangle by the matrix
3. Compute the axis-aligned bounding box of the transformed corners
4. Apply the bounding box to vkCmdSetScissor()
5. Handle edge cases: negative scales, rotations, non-invertible matrices
